sections.text: Valour, glory, firmness, skill, generosity, steadiness in battle and ability to rule - these constitute the duty of a soldier. They flow from his own nature.
Agriculture, protection of the cow and trade are the duty of a trader, again in accordance with his nature. The duty of a servant is to serve, and that too agrees with his nature.
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः।
He who dedicates his actions to the Spirit, without any personal attachment to them, he is no more tainted by sin than the water lily is wetted by water.

We had been discussing chapter 18 and we have so far analyzed the actions, knowledge and the actor. Now, as we have seen, everything is kind of classified into three classes depending on the qualities of the actions, knowledge or the actors. Now we are going into the classification of human beings. We also classified the Sukha, the happiness or the pleasure which comes from your actions. Actions are performed for as we said and discussed many times for two purposes only. One is to gain happiness and other is to avoid unhappiness.
There are actions we perform simply to make sure that there is no sorrow. Your retirement planning for avoiding sorrow in the future, when Im not working, Im not able to work. I need planning for my retirement. Thats for avoiding unhappiness. But I am accumulating money to buy a BMW to get happiness. So there are two reasons we work in this world.
We have identified those. The happiness that comes out of these actions can also be either sattvic happiness. It may take very painful efforts in the beginning, but in the end it will be like nectar. Or it will feel like nectar now, but in the end it turns out to be more painful. Or the last one we have seen is something which in the beginning it is painful, in the end also painful. But I do it because I think thats the only way I can get some comfort.
So now why people act in this manner? The next few verses which we will see said, we are all driven by our qualities. So Bhagavan vastu, pravartate, Beings and things in this world are driven by their own qualities. So if you ask me to go for football match, no matter how hard you try, unless there is some other temptation you give, I wont go to football match. As I said when I was in Dallas, we will have all the social party football matches. The temptation was all the socializing and the food and friends.
Football was least of my concern because its not in my nature. But you have a music party. I will stay hungry if I need to sing. Obviously you cant really sing with a full stomach. So Ill be the last one to eat while everybody has left. Because I want to make sure that I am at my best when my turn comes to sing.
So Im sacrificing something for which my own nature says its pleasurable. So the next few verses it says. nastih prathivyam vyam va divi deveshu va punah sattvam prakruti jai Muktam Yadebhi sat tribhirgunaih. Now first thing they say, well, if I understood all that, Im going to get rid of all the Tamas. Im going to get rid of all the Rajas. Ill be just Sattvik.
Bhagavan said, it is really not possible that there is no being on this earth or again in the heaven. Its our conception that we are the mortal beings on this planet earth and they are immortal beings or devas are in the heaven. These Devas, even you know, Purana says they also have their qualities. Some devas are angry, some manipulate, some do this, you know, thats all the Pura Puranic stories. So it says, there is no being, whether a human being or a divine being, Deva, who is totally liberated from the three qualities. One cannot get rid of these three qualities totally.
Because once you liberate from these Gunas, youre out of the Prakriti, youre out of Maya. These three gunas are the characteristics of Maya, the Prakriti, the manifest world. As long as you are part of the manifest world as a being, these three has to be there. All these three has to be there to make you a being in this world. Therefore, Bhagavan said, there is no being on this planet or anywhere else in this universe who can be liberated completely from these three gunas. The day you transcend all three gunas, there is no Gita class, there is no you, there is no I.
Only the supreme self who was never tainted by this Prakriti remains. So the next verse says Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishyam, Shudranamcha, Parantapa, Karmani, pravibhaktani, svabhava, prabhavaih, gunaih. This is not a social commentary on Indian caste system. Bhagavad Gita was written before the caste system had been polluted by social thinking and historical influences. So this is not a social commentary. Lets not get confused with what happened in India over the last few thousand years regarding the caste system or Varanashram. It simply says Brahmanakshatriya, Vishyam, Shudranamcha, Parantapa Karmani, Pravibhaktani, svabhava, Prabhaivi Gunehi.
Whatever the predominant quality in a being, their karmas are assigned accordingly. If my aptitude is to sing, but then you say no, there is no singing here. Youre going to dance today. Obviously thats not really something I can do. And that happens to me all the time. We go to a party and then everybody starts dancing.
And Im the one who has no real interest at all. But why you are not dancing? Because I dont like dancing. Thats why Im not dancing. So Bhagavan said that each ones actions karma is assigned as per the predominant Gunas. The Brahman, Rakshatriya, Vaishyam or Rakshudra.
Now these classifications are not based on what we understand today; they are based on the Gunas. And we tend to conveniently forget that Bhagavan has already said in the Bhagavad Gita: Chaturvarnam, Maya Shrushta Guna, Karma, Vibhaga Saha. Depending on their gunas, their qualities and their actions, I have created four types of people in this world. Im not a Brahmin and you are not a Shudra. Everybody in this country of 250 million people or so has equal right.
The citizens Im talking about has equal right to be a president of this country. How many in this class wants to be a president of this country? We have no desire to be that. We have no qualities to become one. Does that mean I dont have a right to become a president? You have every right to become a president.
The other day we were at the India festival and Tim Kaine came. Obviously we kind of know him from our association all these years. So we took Medha and had a picture with Tim Kaine. And I said, Senator Kaine, this is the newest member in our family -- the future senator of Virginia. From his perspective, a child can only aspire to become another senator. But Medha will become exactly what her Guna Karma is. So Bhagavan said, the Prakriti has created four types of beings at least in the human race with their qualities and their actions are assigned accordingly.
I told you, in our architecture firm were all architects. We come out of architecture college. But then some have a design tendency on the technical side, some are more on the nitty gritty type -- construction and details. And some are purely management. Now if you take one type and assign them the others work, its always a disaster. So even though we have abolished the system of design department, production department, we still assign work according to their tendencies.
Does that mean we are discriminating? No, we are just trying to make people more comfortable in their ability to produce work. So Bhagavan says Brahmanakshatriya Vishaam Sudranam Chaparantapa Karmani Pravibhaktani. So Bhava prabhavaih gunai hi. All these people have own tendencies and the work is distributed in the society according to their qualities born of their own nature, not just somebody instilled by force. There is a lot of social injustice in this world, but thats not what Bhagavad Gita is about.
Bhagavad Gita makes a statement of facts. How we understand these facts and utilize -- or misuse -- them is a matter of our shortcomings and ignorance. So the next verse says Shamah damah Tapaha Shaucham shanti arjavam Gnanam Vignanam Astikyam Brahma Karma svabhavajam Long list. These are the qualities of the scholarly class thinking class in any society whether it is Indian, tribal or somewhere in some distant planet. More evolved society than human beings. Every society in this age or in Ramas age was divided by people who have tendency to be more thinking, contemplating type, knowledge oriented. Those people who have these qualities -- serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, and also uprightness, knowledge, realization of what is right and wrong.
Realization of what is my true self and what is my non-self. Belief in God -- Brahma Astikyam -- having faith that there is some higher self than this limited self. The Astikyam, Brahma Karma, Svabhavajam -- these are the qualities of the Brahmanas. It does not say the one who was born in a Brahmana family or falls into a Brahmana caste. It simply says that the group of people in any society who have these qualities fall into this type of activity because of their evolution in their intellectual pursuit.
What I know in architecture today is a lot more than I knew in the 1970s. My constant working in that field has given me more and more knowledge. Does that mean that because we should have equal rights, I have to give up my knowledge and act like the guy who comes out of architecture school?
No, this is with my own effort I have achieved a status which is higher than the guy who comes out of architecture school today. So by their own efforts and evolution the people have achieved the state where they have developed these qualities. And we have seen all we are doing is working in our inner equipment through our actions. There are some actions which purify my inner equipment. There are some actions which will pollute my inner equipment. If my actions were consistently to purify my inner equipment I would have developed these qualities.
And those who have done that, they are the Brahmanas. In any society, the next category we discuss is Sauryam Tejo Dhrutihi Daksham Yudde Chapyapalayanam Dhanam Ishwara Bhavasta, Kshatram Karma Svabhavajam. There are people who are scholarly and who have, through the evolution of their mind and intellect, reached a point of serenity and clarity where they can see things as they are. Therefore, in all our Puranas, the king has to go to the Rajguru and ask for advice. Because the king, in his passion, may not see what is right or wrong -- whether to attack that next territory or not. He goes to the Rajguru and asks his counsel.
The Rajguru, because hes not attached, can see things as they are and say, This is good for you, or This is not good for you. This is right or wrong. Because hes devoid of the passion with the King. So the next group of people in any society are the Kshatriyas. We know by now that the Brahmanas do the scholarly work.
Kshatriyas do the political work and protection and administering the country or the kingdom. So their qualities should be prowess, splendor, firmness, dexterity. And also not fleeing from battle -- the battle of life. Some of us run away from any situation when it is threatening, and some will face it head on. The quality of Kshatriya is to face that situation head on. Generosity, lordliness, leadership.
Today we call it leadership qualities. I was part of this leadership Metro Richmond group and so was Rajesh. We want to develop leaders in this community so that they can take this community to the next level. I attended one of the seminars and the guy said something which really I thought was pretty neat. He said, do not work in your business, you have to work on your business. See, my staff works in my business.
I need to be constantly working on my business in a sense that I. I need to have foresight.

The qualities of Kshatriyas (verse 43) include shaurya (valor), teja (brilliance), dhriti (steadfastness), dakshya (skill), apalayana (not fleeing from battle), dana (generosity), and ishvara-bhava (lordly bearing or leadership). For Vaishyas (verse 44): agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade. For Shudras: service. This framework recognizes that different temperaments are suited to different contributions. The key teaching is svabhava-jam - these duties arise from ones own nature, not external imposition.
Verse 45 delivers the crucial promise: sve sve karmani abhirata samsiddhim labhate narah - devoted to ones own duty, a person attains perfection. This is revolutionary: perfection (siddhi) comes not from abandoning your field for a supposedly higher one, but from complete dedication to whatever naturally suits you. A devoted janitor attains the same spiritual perfection as a devoted scholar. The path to liberation is through work, not around it.
Examine your relationship with your work today: Are you doing what naturally suits your temperament, or are you in a field chosen for prestige, family pressure, or financial considerations? If you cannot change your external circumstances, can you change your internal orientation? Even within unsuitable work, find the aspect that aligns with your nature. The teaching promises that wholehearted dedication to ones own dharma - whatever that may be - leads to samsiddhi, complete fulfillment. Where in your current work can you bring more wholehearted presence today?
